  Check Summary Information Sheet

The warrants in the Housing Authority agenda report are for housing assistance payments
made under the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program. The payee has a choice of
receiving the housing assistance payment via direct deposit, which is an electronic fund
transfer made directly to the payee’s bank account, or by paper check.

In the check summary report, the direct deposits are listed first as direct deposits, and then
the checks follow. Each direct deposit and paper check represents payment for 1 to 20
tenants depending upon the number of Section 8 tenants the payee has.

The payee is the property owner or designated management company. The property owner
or manager may be a corporation, partnership, trust, or individual. The payee name is the
owner or manager’s legal business or individual name, which must match Internal Revenue
Service (IRS) records. Here are some common abbreviations used in business names:

LLC = Limited Liability Company

LP = Limited Partnership

DBA = “Doing Business As”

LTD = Limited

Checks made out to the City of Norwalk Housing Authority represent the Family Self
Sufficiency (FSS) escrow deposits. These checks are deposited into the Housing Authority’s
bank account where the funds earn interest and are kept in escrow until the FSS participant
successfully completes the program at which time they receive the balance of their account.

Norwalk Housing Investors, LP is the owner of Center Pointe Villas at 14100 San Antonio
and 11856 Orange. Payments are for Section 8 participants living in these buildings.

Payments to housing authorities, such as the Orange County Housing Authority and San
Bernardino County Housing, represent reimbursements for our participants who have
transferred to those jurisdictions under portability.

Please call Nida Watkins at ext. 5653 if you have any questions.

SUBJECT: PUBLIC HEARING – RESOLUTION NO. NHA-167 ADOPTING PUBLIC
  HOUSING AGENCY ANNUAL PLAN FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23

Background:

Housing authorities are required to complete a five-year Public Housing Agency (PHA)
plan and an annual plan. The purpose of the plans is to advise the United States
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), housing authority participants,
and the general public of the housing authority’s mission for serving the needs of low-
income families. The last five-year plan for the Norwalk Housing Authority (Authority) was
adopted in 2020.

The plan presented tonight is the annual plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2022/23. The plan has
been prepared on HUD’s standardized template.

The annual plan for FY 2022/23 contains the same programs and goals as previous years,
including:
  • Applying for rental vouchers if available;
  • Maintaining high performer status;
  • Utilizing project-based vouchers if the need arises to help preserve and create
  affordable housing;
  • Maximizing the use of available vouchers and funding;
  • Promoting economic self-sufficiency among program participants; and
  • Undertaking affirmative measures to provide a suitable living environment for
  families living in assisted housing regardless of race, color, religion, sex, familial
  status, and disability.
 Housing Authority  March 15, 2022

HUD requires that the public have 45 days to comment on the plan. The draft FY 2022/23
PHA Plan was available for public review starting on January 28, 2022 and all public
comments were due today. The final plan is due to HUD by April 15, 2022.

Fiscal Impact: N/A

Citizens Advised:

A notice was published in The Norwalk Patriot on January 28, 2022 announcing the
availability of the plan for public review and comment and the March 15, 2022 public
hearing date.

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 2: Improve living
conditions for residents in greatest need.

Purpose. The 5-Year and Annual PHA Plans provide a ready source for interested parties to locate basic PHA policies, rules, and requirements concerning
the PHA’s operations, programs, and services, including changes to these policies, and informs HUD, families served by the PHA, and members of the
public of the PHA’s mission, goals and objectives for serving the needs of low- income, very low- income, and extremely low- income families

Applicability. The Form HUD-50075-HCV is to be completed annually by HCV-Only PHAs. PHAs that meet the definition of a Standard PHA, Troubled
PHA, High Performer PHA, Small PHA, or Qualified PHA do not need to submit this form. Where applicable, separate Annual PHA Plan forms are
available for each of these types of PHAs.

Definitions.

(1) High-Performer PHA – A PHA that owns or manages more than 550 combined public housing units and housing choice vouchers, and was designated as a
  high performer on both the most recent Public Housing Assessment System (PHAS) and Section Eight Management Assessment Program (SEMAP)
  assessments if administering both programs, or PHAS if only administering public housing.
(2)  Small PHA - A PHA that is not designated as PHAS or SEMAP troubled, that owns or manages less than 250 public housing units and any number of vouchers
  where the total combined units exceed 550.
(3)  Housing Choice Voucher (HCV) Only PHA - A PHA that administers more than 550 HCVs, was not designated as troubled in its most recent SEMAP
  assessment and does not own or manage public housing.
(4)  Standard PHA - A PHA that owns or manages 250 or more public housing units and any number of vouchers where the total combined units exceed 550, and
  that was designated as a standard performer in the most recent PHAS and SEMAP assessments.
(5)  Troubled PHA - A PHA that achieves an overall PHAS or SEMAP score of less than 60 percent.
(6)  Qualified PHA - A PHA with 550 or fewer public housing dwelling units and/or housing choice vouchers combined and is not PHAS or SEMAP troubled.

B.2  New Activities.

  The Housing Authority will continue to administer up to 40 project-based vouchers at Soroptimist Village, which are
  under contract through June 30, 2027 and may dedicate up to 100 additional vouchers to other units under the project-
  based voucher program. Projects will be located in census tracts with poverty rates under the City’s current poverty
  rate or in/adjacent to the City’s economic opportunity nodes. The City of Norwalk has aging housing stock, high rents,
  and limited rental housing choices. As such, project-based vouchers are an appropriate option to facilitate the
  development of new rental housing or projects that create new housing opportunities for special needs populations,
  particularly for the homeless or individuals with disabilities. Additionally, project-based vouchers are a tool for
  preserving affordable housing that is at risk of converting to market-rate housing and for meeting program utilization
  goals in a tight rental market. Project-basing vouchers is consistent with the 5-year PHA Plan as it is one of the
  strategies listed in the Plan to address housing needs by utilizing project-based vouchers to increase the supply of
  assisted housing and supports the PHA Plan goal of maximizing leasing and budget utilization.

  Page 2 of 7  form HUD-50075-HCV (03/31/2024)
 B.3  Progress Report.

  Provide a description of the PHA’s progress in meeting its Mission and Goals described in its 5-Year PHA Plan.

  Goal #1: Apply for additional rental vouchers should funding become available.
  Progress: There have been no opportunities to apply for new regular tenant-based vouchers. The authority will
  continue to seek for opportunities as they become available. However, in May 2021, the NHA did receive 46
  Emergency Housing Vouchers (EHV’s) funding as authorized by the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021.

  Goal #2: Maintain high performing status.
  Progress: The Housing Authority received high performer designation for its performance in FY 2015/16, 2016/17 &
  2017/18. The NHA has applied for a SEMAP waiver (Notice PIH 2021-34) which waives the application of SEMAP
  in its entirety.

  Goal #3: Maximize leasing and budget utilization.
  Progress: The Authority is experiencing a shortage of available units in the City of Norwalk due to the eviction
  moratorium. Participants are struggling to find units to lease-up. The Authority staff called every single property
  owner that listed with our Business Licensing Department to promote our program and to see if we could match
  vacancies with voucher holders. The Authority followed up by mailing flyers and advertising in the Norwalk Patriot
  and on all social media platforms. In addition, the Authority is purging its waitlist and extending the term of the
  vouchers. To summarize our utilization rate has dropped. The Authority is planning to organize a mass waitlist pull
  and lease-up as soon as the COVID surge is under control. Lastly, the Authority is working on increasing its payment
  standards to a 110% of the HUD published fair market rents to be able to compete with the current high market rents.
  The Authority is hoping that it will be able to maximize its leasing with all these efforts.

  Goal #4: Promote economic self-sufficiency among program participants.
  Progress: The Authority continues to administer the Family Self Sufficiency (FSS) program with 13 slots. The
  Authority received FSS Grant funding for the past five years. The Authority strengthened its partnership with the
  Southeast Los Angeles County Workforce Development Board by approving a new Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) on August 15, 2017 and updated MOU on June 18, 2019. The Authority continues to maintain partnerships
  with Cerritos College and the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District. Information about job opportunities,
  training, job fairs, and scholarships are shared with FSS participants throughout the year. The Authority also serves on
  the System Management Team for the local America’s Job Center of California (AJCC).

  Goal #5: Undertake affirmative measures to provide a suitable living environment for families living in assisted
  housing, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, familiar status, and disability.
  Progress: The program is promoted to all segments of the Norwalk population. Housing Quality Standards are
  applied equally to all units regardless of location or family type. The Authority provides more housing search time to
  disabled households and reviews reasonable accommodation requests on a case-by-case basis. The Authority works
  closely with the Fair Housing Foundation to assist participants with fair housing issues and to provide fair housing
  training to landlords. The Housing Authority also participated in the development of the City’s 2015 and 2020
  Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice.

  D.1 Affirmatively Furthering Fair Housing. The PHA will use the answer blocks in item D.1 to provide a statement of its strategies and actions to implement
  each fair housing goal outlined in its accepted Assessment of Fair Housing (AFH) consistent with 24 CFR § 5.154(d)(5) that states, in relevant part: “To
  implement goals and priorities in an AFH, strategies and actions shall be included in program participants' … PHA Plans (including any plans incorporated
  therein) …. Strategies and actions must affirmatively further fair housing ….” Use the chart provided to specify each fair housing goal from the PHA’s AFH for
  which the PHA is the responsible program participant – whether the AFH was prepared solely by the PHA, jointly with one or more other PHAs, or in
  collaboration with a state or local jurisdiction – and specify the fair housing strategies and actions to be implemented by the PHA during the period covered by
  this PHA Plan. If there are more than three fair housing goals, add answer blocks as necessary.

  Until such time as the PHA is required to submit an AFH, the PHA will not have to complete section D., nevertheless, the PHA will address its obligation to
  affirmatively further fair housing in part by fulfilling the requirements at 24 CFR 903.7(o)(3) enacted prior to August 17, 2015, which means that it examines its
  own programs or proposed programs; identifies any impediments to fair housing choice within those programs; addresses those impediments in a reasonable
  fashion in view of the resources available; works with local jurisdictions to implement any of the jurisdiction’s initiatives to affirmatively further fair housing
  that require the PHA’s involvement; and maintain records reflecting these analyses and actions. Furthermore, under Section 5A(d)(15) of the U.S. Housing Act
  of 1937, as amended, a PHA must submit a civil rights certification with its Annual PHA Plan, which is described at 24 CFR 903.7(o)(1) except for qualified
  PHAs who submit the Form HUD-50077-CR as a standalone document.
